overview.summary: This Node.js Express API implements the RealWorld spec with TypeScript and Prisma ORM against PostgreSQL. It exposes REST routes for articles, auth, profiles, and tags, uses JWT authentication with bcrypt password hashing, and includes Jest tests plus Nx tooling.

modules.name: Application entry and middleware
modules.role: Creates the Express app, applies CORS and body parsing, mounts all API routes, serves static assets, and starts the HTTP server on a port from env vars.
modules.whyItExists: Centralizes app bootstrap so the server has one place to configure middleware, error handling, and listening, keeping concerns separated from route logic.

modules.name: Route aggregation
modules.role: Mounts tag, article, profile, and auth controllers under the /api prefix using Express Router.
modules.whyItExists: Provides a single registration point for all API route groups so main.ts only needs to import one routes module.

modules.name: Articles module
modules.role: Handles article CRUD, feed, comments, favorites, and tag listing through controller endpoints backed by service logic.
modules.whyItExists: Groups article-related HTTP handling and business rules together so changes to articles do not touch auth, profile, or tag code.

modules.name: Authentication module
modules.role: Registers and logs in users, issues JWT tokens, verifies tokens for protected routes, and attaches user info to requests.
modules.whyItExists: Isolates identity and access concerns so other modules can require authentication through a shared auth middleware without duplicating token logic.

modules.name: Profiles module
modules.role: Retrieves user profiles and follows or unfollows other users.
modules.whyItExists: Keeps social profile behavior separate from article and authentication logic.

modules.name: Tags module
modules.role: Returns the list of available tags used for filtering articles.
modules.whyItExists: Provides a small dedicated endpoint for tag discovery instead of mixing it into article controllers.

modules.name: Database and ORM
modules.role: Defines the PostgreSQL schema, generates the Prisma Client, applies migrations, and seeds initial data.
modules.whyItExists: Centralizes data modeling and schema evolution so services query through a typed ORM instead of raw SQL.

modules.name: Configuration and tooling
modules.role: Declares dependencies, TypeScript compiler options, Jest test setup, Docker image build instructions, and lint/format rules.
modules.whyItExists: Separates environment and build configuration from application code so the same source can be tested, built, and deployed consistently.

30b68e1e881462b2f4164ea09ab4c4f5699c7b0b.title: Add user id field to getCurrentUser query
30b68e1e881462b2f4164ea09ab4c4f5699c7b0b.whatChanged: Added `id: true` to the select object in the `getCurrentUser` function so the database query now returns the user's id along with email, username, and bio.
30b68e1e881462b2f4164ea09ab4c4f5699c7b0b.whyItMatters: Without `id: true`, the query omitted the user id, so callers could not identify which user was returned.
30b68e1e881462b2f4164ea09ab4c4f5699c7b0b.designReasoning: The function already selected specific fields instead of returning the whole user record, so adding `id: true` keeps the same field-selection pattern while including the missing identifier.
30b68e1e881462b2f4164ea09ab4c4f5699c7b0b.tradeoffs: Returning one extra column adds a negligible amount of data transfer but prevents callers from needing a separate lookup to learn the user's id.
alternatives: Select all fields instead of listing them individually
Return the id from a separate query after fetching the user

88b258ce54aaf54ff52511ba26edd52e36df201e.title: Update documentation and seed configuration
88b258ce54aaf54ff52511ba26edd52e36df201e.whatChanged: README.md gained instructions to run database migrations with `npx prisma migrate deploy`. package.json changed the Prisma seed command from `tsx` to `ts-node` with CommonJS options and made the schema path relative. src/main.ts switched Express and CORS imports from namespace style to default imports. src/prisma/seed.ts changed `main` from an exported function to a local constant and reduced seed data from 30 users with 20 articles each to 12 users with 12 articles each.
88b258ce54aaf54ff52511ba26edd52e36df201e.whyItMatters: The README now documents how to apply SQL migrations, which helps new developers set up the database. The seed changes reduce the amount of generated test data, likely to make local seeding faster and lighter. The import style change aligns with default import syntax used elsewhere in the file.
88b258ce54aaf54ff52511ba26edd52e36df201e.designReasoning: The project uses Prisma as an ORM to manage database schema and seed data. Separating migration instructions in README keeps setup steps visible. Reducing seed counts limits database load during development while still providing enough sample data.
88b258ce54aaf54ff52511ba26edd52e36df201e.tradeoffs: Fewer seed records mean faster setup but less coverage for testing pagination or large datasets. Switching to `ts-node` with transpile-only may speed up startup but skips type checking during seed execution.
alternatives: Keep 30 users and 20 articles per user
Use namespace imports for Express and CORS

Changed main export to const and reduced array lengths from 30 and 20 to 12

a981fd9a6be13d665688c50f16a0f8da2b3394d9.title: Migrate from Express/Mongoose to Nx/Prisma monorepo
a981fd9a6be13d665688c50f16a0f8da2b3394d9.whatChanged: Removed old Express app files such as app.js, config/index.js, config/passport.js, and CI configs like .circleci/config.yml and .travis.yml. Added Nx configuration files including .eslintrc.json, .prettierrc, .prettierignore, Dockerfile, and updated README.md to describe Prisma instead of Mongoose. Updated .gitignore to include Nx cache and dist folders.
a981fd9a6be13d665688c50f16a0f8da2b3394d9.whyItMatters: The project switched database tooling from Mongoose to Prisma and adopted the Nx monorepo tooling for building, testing, and containerizing the API. This changes how developers install, run, seed, and deploy the application.
a981fd9a6be13d665688c50f16a0f8da2b3394d9.designReasoning: Nx provides a standardized way to manage multiple projects, run tasks, and generate Docker images in one repository. Prisma is used as an ORM to map database tables to TypeScript objects, replacing Mongoose's MongoDB modeling. Separate ESLint configs for TypeScript and JavaScript keep linting rules matched to file type.
a981fd9a6be13d665688c50f16a0f8da2b3394d9.tradeoffs: Adopting Nx adds build tooling complexity and requires learning new commands such as npx nx serve api. Switching from Mongoose to Prisma means the data layer and connection strings change, and old CI files were removed so the continuous integration setup must be reconfigured elsewhere.
alternatives: Keep the original Express + Mongoose structure with CircleCI and Travis CI
Use a different monorepo tool such as Turborepo instead of Nx
Use a different ORM such as Sequelize or Drizzle instead of Prisma

5eeccf13f3a5778b8ba818240edf89919a689a80.title: Update demo app to use Prisma and user IDs instead of usernames
5eeccf13f3a5778b8ba818240edf89919a689a80.whatChanged: The README now documents Prisma setup instead of Mongoose, and package.json points the Prisma seed and schema to ./src/prisma/. In article.controller.ts, calls to getArticles, getFeed, createArticle, getArticle, updateArticle, deleteArticle, and getCommentsByArticle now pass req.auth?.user?.id instead of req.auth?.user?.username. The .gitignore now excludes .env.
5eeccf13f3a5778b8ba818240edf89919a689a80.whyItMatters: Switching from usernames to user IDs means article and comment lookups rely on a stable database identifier rather than a value a user could change, which helps keep ownership checks correct. Adding .env to .gitignore keeps database URLs and JWT secrets out of version control.
5eeccf13f3a5778b8ba818240edf89919a689a80.designReasoning: The app follows a client-server design where Express routes handle HTTP requests and Prisma maps data to a database schema. Using user.id for ownership checks separates authentication (who signed in) from authorization (whether they own the article), which is a separation-of-concerns pattern.
5eeccf13f3a5778b8ba818240edf89919a689a80.tradeoffs: User IDs are stable but less human-readable than usernames in logs or debugging. Ignoring .env improves security but requires developers to create the file locally and set variables on the host provider manually.
alternatives: Keep using usernames for ownership checks
Store secrets in code instead of .env

Prisma seed and schema paths changed from ./prisma/ to ./src/prisma/
Multiple route handlers now pass req.auth?.user?.id instead of req.auth?.user?.username

e40aeb924bbadca7f6444b502bdb7b1e6eddb8f9.title: Migrate project to Nx build system
e40aeb924bbadca7f6444b502bdb7b1e6eddb8f9.whatChanged: Removed CircleCI and Travis CI configuration files, deleted the old Express app entry point (app.js), config files, and models/routes setup, and added Nx configuration files including eslint, prettier, gitignore, Dockerfile, README, e2e project, jest config, and a sample e2e test.
e40aeb924bbadca7f6444b502bdb7b1e6eddb8f9.whyItMatters: The project switches to Nx, a build system that provides local caching and standardized task running, which can speed up builds and tests by avoiding repeated work.
e40aeb924bbadca7f6444b502bdb7b1e6eddb8f9.designReasoning: Nx organizes code into projects with targets defined in project.json and uses executors such as @nx/jest:jest and @nx/eslint:lint to run tests and linting consistently across the workspace.
e40aeb924bbadca7f6444b502bdb7b1e6eddb8f9.tradeoffs: Gains faster builds through caching and a unified command structure, but loses the previous simple Node/Express server setup and CI files, requiring teams to learn Nx commands and reconfigure deployment.
alternatives: Keep the original CircleCI and Travis CI configs
Use a plain package.json scripts setup without Nx
Use another monorepo tool such as Turborepo or Lerna
